newsitem.title: CHINA: China defence minister leaves for United States.
newsitem.headline: China defence minister leaves for United States.

text.p: China's Defence Minister Chi Haotian left on Monday for the United States, saying he was confident of promoting understanding, friendship and cooperation between the two powers.
Chi's long-delayed 10-day visit is at the invitation of U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, the official Xinhua news agency said, returning a visit by Perry to China in October 1994.
Chi's U.S. trip was postponed twice because of tension between the two powers over Taiwan.

The two will discuss bilateral military issues, as well as global and Asia-Pacific security matters of mutual concern, Xinhua said, adding that Chi would tour military academies and meet senior U.S. officials.

But U.S. and Chinese leaders have moved to improve ties in recent weeks. Those steps have included a visit to Beijing by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and talks between Chinese President Jiang Zemin and U.S. President Bill Clinton at a meeting of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Philippines last month.

Before his departure, Chi was quoted by Xinhua as saying he was "imbued with confidence" and believed he would accomplish his goal of "promoting understanding, developing friendship and strengthening cooperation" between the two sides.
Sino-U.S. ties have long been battered by disputes over Taiwan, human rights, copyright piracy, arms sales and alleged nuclear proliferation.
Relations between the two sides soured in March when China conducted missile tests off the coast of Taiwan during the run-up to the island's first direct presidential election.
Washington responded by sending two aircraft carrier battle groups to the area, a move that infuriated Beijing.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
